test_title: PYST 24 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 21 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

She exclaimed with disgust that the food tasted terrible.

options.text: She said, "Alas! This food tastes terrible."
She said, "Ugh! How terrible this food tastes!"
She exclaimed, "Oh no! This food tastes terrible!"

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She exclaimed with disgust that the food tasted terrible.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"She exclaimed with disgust" becomes "Ugh!"**
 
 
• The expression "Ugh!" conveys the disgust mentioned in the indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **"the food tasted terrible" becomes "How terrible this food tastes!"**
 
 
• The phrase is converted into a direct exclamation to match the tone and meaning.
 
• The verb tense is adjusted for direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with an exclamation "Ugh!" followed by a complete sentence expressing disgust.
 
• Maintains the tone and meaning of the original indirect speech.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said, "Ugh! How terrible this food tastes!"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Alas! This food tastes terrible."

 
 
• The word "Alas" expresses sadness rather than disgust, altering the tone.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Oh no! This food tastes terrible."
 
 
• The phrase "Oh no" conveys surprise or concern, which doesn't match the disgust in the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "What terrible-tasting food!"
 
 
• Although it conveys disgust, the sentence structure is different and doesn't match the original sentence fully.
